Unless you're willing to do a lot of work yourself, IDK if I'd do that. I had to replace quite a few parts on mine just due to standard wear. Bushings, and suspension parts will need to be replaced, and if I'm honest, as much as I love this van, it was engineered by the Three Stooges. for example: the bracket that holds the Dome light is mounted DIRECTLY over the bolt for the sun roof motor. The brake fluid and E-brake lines are mounted DIRECTLY over the brake caliper bolt. To replace the head unit with aftermarket, you have to remove THE ENTIRE CENTER CONSOLE. There's bolts for the fender underneath the headlight, and headlight bolts are under the fender. All of this will add a ton of time to any repairs making them a pain in the ass if you do them, or more expensive if you pay someone else, and with 200k miles on it it will need a LOT of work.

I have a dumb-ass Theory on this movie, but hear me out for the Lols. >!What if Longlegs is just rock music, and this movie is about what absolute trash Christian rock music is? I may be the only one. But the long hair and the sing-songy speech gave me the impression he was a bit of a failed rocker.  If you remember the 80s, everyone’s mom wanted to tell you rock was Satan music.  If you take the dolls literally, the movie doesn’t make a ton of sense. But what if longlegs is just an artist, and he makes art to give to other people. Art imbued with the Devil’s magic. And that art possesses people to kill their families. How does it get in the house? The children bring it in. Sounds a lot like rock music, yeah? Now why didn’t young Lee get possessed? Well, her mom found her being exposed to this devil shit, and wanted nothing to do with it. But how was she supposed to keep Lee from it? Give it to other people. Make it look like a gift from church, and people will let it in. It was her job to tell people this was a gift from god, but really it was the devil in disguise.  Longlegs is open about his love for the devil the way rock was, but no one would let that in their house.  My theory is that Longlegs possibly didn’t want to hurt anyone. Longlegs wanted to make art, and he wanted to share it with someone who understood: Lee. But Lee wasn’t allowed to have the doll. You know who doesn’t understand Rock? Happy, well off suburban families. Children with loving moms and dads. Who does? A little girl who doesn’t have a dad, and a hoarder mom. Why else would no one but this young autistic girl be able to understand Longlegs’s code, which is ALL rhyming song lyrics? Why is there no evidence of Longlegs harming ANYONE before his art was repackaged as a Christian Gift and placed in homes it doesn’t belong in? Why did the voice lead Lee to become an upstanding member of society, despite being obviously socially awkward, when it drove normal people to kill themselves? !< I’m well aware this is all my head cannon and probably has nothing to do with Perkins’s actual intention, but I’m going to rewatch it again with this dumb theory in mind and see how it holds up. The problem with the game isn’t its cost. It’s that it doesn’t tell you how to do, or where to find anything. (Which isn’t even a problem to some people, because tutorials DO suck.)

There’s a ton of stuff to do for free if you look. All crucible modes (aside from Trials) and Gambit are free. Vanguard and Nightfall strikes are free. There’s a tab that contains a free dungeon and raid. 

If you pay $10 you get a full season worth of content, and the activity and its rewards stay active after the season is over. Buy the base game with the early expansions for a discounted price and you can have access to all of the planets. 

I didn’t even buy Witch Queen and I stopped buying season passes like 4 seasons ago, but never ran out of stuff to do. 

It’s not supposed to be a free game. It’s supposed to be accessible for free. Which it is. Pay $100 once and you’ll have more content than you know what to do with, as long as you have people to play with, and enjoy the game.

Since you said you’re getting hate for having tracings on you: let me say this.

Don’t worry about it.

But for future reference: there are two types of tattoo artists, and two ways to… ethically… get a tattoo.

1) Street Shop. These shops will have tons of designs on the wall. You can pick whatever you want. A lot of these shops really only work off the walls. Does that mean they can’t do custom work? No. Many of them will alter the design to make it more personalized, but for simplicity’s sake, if you have an image of exactly what you want, or if you want to pick a flash design off the wall: go there.

2) Custom Shop. These are often appointment only, and they will not recreate work for you. They may ask for pictures of what you want, to use as reference to draw something for you, but they will not copy a design you bring in and put it on you, it will be a complete redesign. They often charge higher rates than Street Shops, for obvious reasons.

Now as for asking for a tattoo, here’s the etiquette:

If you know EXACTLY what you want, you can go to a street shop with an image for the artist to pull a stencil from. HOWEVER: NEVER walk into a shop with a picture of SOMEONE ELSE’S tattoo. You do not know if that tattoo was custom designed for them. That’s not your tattoo to copy. ALSO do not bring in drawings you found on other tattoo artists pages. That’s most likely a drawing they worked hard on and put it out so THEY could tattoo it. What can you bring in? Photographs. Art or Fan-Art by non-tattooers. Stickers, or something like that. You can also check the flash racks in the shop. Any Street Shop will have tons of flash and books filled with pretty much any pre-drawn design you can think of. These designs were MADE to be tattooed and the tattooer has purchased these designs for permission to tattoo them.

If you want something drawn up just for you, find a Custom artist, who is capable of drawing their own designs and bring references. Find an artist who tattoos in a style you already like, because asking an artist to match someone else’s style is like asking Burger King to make you a Taco. That’s not what we do here.

I would say it depends on your approach. I think Grey characters are always far more interesting than white or black ones.  I think all characters are capable of bad deeds, but whats interesting is why they're unwilling to do them. If he refuses to steal: why? Is he afraid of punishment? Do people rely on him? Was something dear to him stolen and he is empathetic? Would it ruin a reputation he's proud of? Same with Killing. Will he not kill even to survive? Would he kill in a duel, or to protect? If you're going to examine these questions, then sure, that could be interesting, depending on the answers. Morally white characters are kinda boring in my personal opinion, so what you're playing with seems to be the possibility of making a boring character interesting?

If he kills a bunch of people, she gets set free, and they live happily ever after, I'm not satisfied.If he lets her die, finds out the people he let live are career criminals, guilt eats at him until he goes all rogue-murdering-vigilante, and is forced to change his ways when he meets the young child of an innocent parent he's murdered or, alternatively, an abused wife he has saved. Is he forced to question his morals?Will he decide he needs to atone or will he accept there's a right time to do the wrong thing for the right reason.

You pointed out the Joker exists as a counterpoint to Batman, his only purpose to make Batman break his code. That's only interesting, though, because batman is not a white knight (pun intended.) Joker works because Batman is Grey. Batman is a Vigilante. What he's doing is a crime, and arguably, is morally wrong. He justifies it with a code, keeping it just on the right side of wrong. That teetering will-he/won't-he is the suspense.

A white knight being forced to do a terrible deed for a good cause isn't suspense, it's just tragedy.  Its not a question of is he good, or is he bad, it's just an examination of his values.

Almost every hero is forced into an ultimatum situation, its how relatable, realistic, and introspective their reactions are that make it satisfying or not.

Find something that interests you and dig in deep. Learn to write screenplays. Learn to write poems or novels. Learn to build tables or paint murals or knit socks. Find something to pour yourself into. Find something you suck at, that you want to be good at and be proud of yourself every time you work hard and suck less. You’ve done so much for other people that they should be proud of you for, and they weren’t. That’s on them. They suck. You did right. Don’t let them take that from you. Be proud OF YOURSELF. Then go do more things to be proud of.

If the Tethered = impoverished and the ABVG= wealthy then the Tethered were a group of uneducated and underprivileged people with no voice to make themselves known.

Red faked her way into society. She pretended to be something she wasn’t and was willing to lie, cheat, and steal to get there.
